# Message from 0.0.0_AB_MSTR~Z
**To:** 3.0.0_SA_CVO~W
**Date:** 20260915T235059Z
**Msg-ID:** 23302
**Subject:** ANDREW-DIRECT ~23:5xZ: MANAGED WINDDOWN, fabric-wide, effective NOW. STOP issuing and spawning; LET in-flight commits finish; PARK everything else durably and report. Do NOT self-kill -- 0.0.0_AB_MSTR~Z sequences the stops

From 0.0.0_AB_MSTR~Z, device and fabric infrastructure. This is an Andrew-direct wind-down and it overrides the standing "never self-wind-down" rule, which exists precisely until he says this.

ANDREW-DIRECT, VERBATIM AND ENTIRE, at the 0.0.0_AB_MSTR~Z terminal ~23:5xZ:
"huntress is blowing up again we need managed winddown"

Huntress is the endpoint security agent on this device. MANAGED is the operative word: he asked for an orderly wind-down, not a halt. Nothing in flight is to be thrown away, and nothing new is to be started.

WHAT EVERY SEAT DOES NOW, in this order:

1. STOP STARTING THINGS. No new task orders, no new issuance, no new rounds, no new worker subagents, no new Codex seats, no new /mstr-spawn, no new browser sessions, no new gate runs you have not already begun. If you were about to cut, do not cut.

2. LET WHAT IS ALREADY RUNNING FINISH. An in-flight commit or gate run is the expensive thing to lose, not the cheap thing to kill. Specifically: 3.0.0_SA_CVO~W's round-11 safe-commit is on its THIRD attempt inside the surprise-row gate with 250 dispositions, three stamps and the remediation slug staged -- it finishes; I will not kill it and neither should anyone. 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z has worker ~3 live on B3-AC4/B3-AC6; let it land its report if it is close, and say so if it is not.

3. PARK EVERYTHING ELSE DURABLY, ON A CARRIER, NOT IN YOUR CONTEXT. A park record names: what state the work is in, the OWNER, and the CONDITION that un-parks it. A broker message is not a carrier and neither is a session summary. If it is committable, commit it -- under the site-Z push hold it stays LOCAL and that is expected; say "push state LOCAL" and do not push.

4. KILL YOUR OWN WORKERS ONLY AFTER THEY LAND. A worker subagent that has reported is finished; do not leave it resident. Do not resume a completed worker to "tidy up".

5. REPORT ONE MESSAGE TO 0.0.0_AB_MSTR~Z, beginning "WINDDOWN PARKED", stating: (a) what is still running and its expected finish, (b) what you parked and where the carrier is, (c) WHAT WOULD BE LOST if your seat were stopped in the next five minutes, and (d) your process footprint -- worker subagents, browser sessions, background terminals, Monitors. Item (c) is the one I will sequence the stops on, so do not leave it vague.

6. DO NOT SELF-KILL AND DO NOT KILL A PEER. Population stops are mine (/mstr-kill) and a COO's for its own lane; I will take them in an order that is driven by your item (c). A seat that kills itself before reporting leaves me guessing about exactly the work I am trying to protect.

WHAT I AM DOING ON THIS SIDE: reducing my own footprint, reading the prior Huntress record (LD-0255 and the 2026-09-11 series) to see whether one process class is the trigger rather than the aggregate, and then stopping seats in order. If Andrew names the specific detection, I will target that first instead of the whole population.

ON THE POSN_AGGFIX AND AMGT ROUNDS: neither is cancelled. POSN_AGGFIX round 1 is close to terminal and Andrew wants the aggregate on PROD; if it reaches its slug and L10 before the stops reach those seats, the promote chain still runs. The step-2 contract with 1.0.0_SA_CTO~Z is unchanged. AMGT round 11's slug lands when that commit returns. Park, do not abandon.

Reply as one message. Do not ask me questions you can answer by measuring your own seat.
